{
  "research_question": "Does the stimulation paradigm (Combined, ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only, Sham) have a statistically significant effect on mouse navigation performance metrics (Time-to-Target, Success, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, and Angular Dispersion)?",
  "stim_paradigms_compared": ["Combined", "ICMS Only", "Dim Visual Only", "Bright Visual Only", "Sham"],
  "response_variables": ["Time-to-Target", "Success", "Path Efficiency", "Average Speed", "AD"],
  "anova_plan": [
    "For Time-to-Target: Perform a one-way ANOVA with 'Stim Paradigm' as the fixed factor to test for mean differences across the five groups.",
    "For Success: Perform a one-way ANOVA with 'Stim Paradigm' as the fixed factor to test for mean differences (treating the binary outcome as continuous for the omnibus test).",
    "For Path Efficiency: Perform a one-way ANOVA with 'Stim Paradigm' as the fixed factor to test for mean differences.",
    "For Average Speed: Perform a one-way ANOVA with 'Stim Paradigm' as the fixed factor to test for mean differences.",
    "For AD: Perform a one-way ANOVA with 'Stim Paradigm' as the fixed factor to test for mean differences in angular dispersion."
  ],
  "assumptions_and_diagnostics": [
    "Verify Normality: Check residuals of each response variable for normality using Q-Q plots and Shapiro-Wilk tests, as ANOVA is sensitive to non-normality, especially with the skewed distribution of Time-to-Target (skewed right) and bounded variables like Success and AD.",
    "Verify Homogeneity of Variances: Conduct Levene's test for equality of variances across the five stimulation paradigms for each response variable.",
    "Check Independence: Ensure observations are independent; given the 'Mouse' column has 8 levels, verify that multiple trials per mouse do not induce pseudoreplication or use a mixed-effects model if trials are nested within mice.",
    "Address Non-Normality/Boundedness: If residuals are non-normal or variances are unequal, consider data transformations (e.g., log for Time-to-Target, arcsine square root for Success and AD) or use non-parametric alternatives (Kruskal-Wallis H test)."
  ],
  "posthoc_plan": [
    "If the omnibus ANOVA F-test is significant for any response variable, proceed with pairwise comparisons.",
    "Use Tukey's HSD (Honestly Significant Difference) test for all pairwise comparisons between the five stimulation paradigms to control the family-wise error rate.",
    "For Time-to-Target, given the likely skew, perform post-hoc comparisons on transformed data or use non-parametric pairwise tests (e.g., Dunn's test with Bonferroni correction) if normality cannot be achieved post-transformation.",
    "Report effect sizes (e.g., eta-squared) for significant findings."
  ],
  "expected_findings": [
    "Time-to-Target: Combined stimulation may reduce time-to-target compared to Sham or ICMS Only, given the large sample size for Combined (n=48846) suggests robust learning or performance.",
    "Success: Combined or ICMS Only paradigms may yield higher success rates compared to Dim Visual Only or Bright Visual Only if visual cues are critical for navigation.",
    "Path Efficiency: Combined stimulation may result in more direct paths (higher efficiency) compared to single-modality stimulations.",
    "Average Speed: Combined stimulation may increase average speed compared to Sham, indicating improved motor planning or confidence.",
    "AD (Angular Dispersion): Combined stimulation may reduce angular dispersion (lower AD) compared to Sham, indicating more consistent navigation trajectories."
  ],
  "limitations": [
    "Potential pseudoreplication: The dataset contains multiple trials per mouse (8 mouse levels), but the planned one-way ANOVA treats rows as independent. This violates the independence assumption if trials are not independent within a mouse.",
    "Skewed distributions: Time-to-Target has a wide range (0.5 to 201.39) and likely right-skewed distribution, violating ANOVA normality assumptions without transformation.",
    "Bounded variables: Success (0-1) and AD (0-1) are bounded, which can lead to heteroscedasticity (variance depends on the mean), violating ANOVA assumptions.",
    "Unbalanced design: The number of observations per stimulation paradigm is highly unequal (e.g., Combined n=48846 vs. Bright Visual Only n=3323), which can affect the power and validity of the F-test."
  ],
  "recommended_next_analysis": "Fit a linear mixed-effects model (LMM) for each response variable with 'Stim Paradigm' as a fixed effect and 'Mouse' as a random intercept to account for repeated measures, followed by likelihood ratio tests or parametric bootstrapping for inference, with appropriate transformations for non-Gaussian residuals."
}
